newsitem.title: UK: North Sea cod stocks in danger, report finds.
newsitem.headline: North Sea cod stocks in danger, report finds.

text.p: Fishermen are catching too much cod in the North Sea and if they continue to do so the breed's population could collapse, a team of experts said on Wednesday.

"Without a substantial reduction in the rate of fishing, the North Sea cod stock may well collapse," Robin Cook, a fisheries expert at Britain's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food and colleagues in Iceland and Canada predicted.

"There is a need for swift and effective action to protect the stock and avoid the problems of the much-publicised collapse of cod stocks off the coast of Atlantic Canada," they reported in the science journal Nature.
That collapse forced a complete ban on cod fishing off Canada's east coast in 1992. Canadian officials predict it could take up to 15 years for the stocks to recover.
As many as 60 percent of all cod in the North Sea are taken by trawlers every year.

The International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES), which advises fishery managers on fish stocks in the northeast Atlantic, has recommended that trawler fleets immediately cut back their cod harvests by 20 to 30 percent to allow populations to recover. But this has not happened.

"Our analysis suggests that not only is the present exploitation rate unsustainable, but that even regimens close to the maximum sustainable yield may be potentially prone to risk," Cook's group wrote. Fishing was so heavy that populations were unable to replace themselves, Cook, a member of ICES, said.

"Cod can live many years and only reach maturity in significant numbers by the age of four. However, fish are caught as early as age one and by age two young fish are fully exploited by the fishery," he wrote.
This meant that fish are killed off before they can reproduce -- a recipe for disaster.

Cod could never be fully protected, because when trawlers go after other bottom-dwelling fish such as haddock and whiting they will inevitably catch cod, too. The researchers suggested the need to cut back overall, perhaps with quotas of a "direct reduction in fishing activity."
Several countries, including Britain, Denmark, Belgium, Germany, France and Netherlands, have North Sea cod quotas.
